purpose: Let the Codex thread act as the model hub for product-image to brand-film-spec work. The repository provides templates, schemas, deterministic gates, and artifact contracts; Codex owns image understanding, creative reasoning, scoring judgment, and final spec writing.

responsibilities: inspect one or more product images supplied in the Codex thread
convert visual facts into the existing feature and creative-brief contracts
generate, critique, shortlist, and select the creative route
write the final brand-film-spec markdown and companion report
optionally call imagegen for keyframe previsualization assets

model_policy.reason: The Codex branch workflow should not split image understanding, creative generation, judging, and final writing across unrelated LLM/VLM services.

optional_plugins.use: Generate 3-5 still keyframes or visual-risk probes before sending a spec to the expensive video renderer.
optional_plugins.boundary: Imagegen may create preview assets, but Codex still owns the product-fidelity review and final render decision.

required.name: product_images
required.description: One or more product images sent by the user in the Codex thread or referenced by local path/URL.

instructions: Treat uploaded images as the highest-priority source of truth.
If multiple images conflict, call out the conflict and prefer the primary product image for final product facts.
Do not infer unverifiable brand history, sales numbers, or awards.
Produce category, sub_category, product_name, selling_points, target_audience, dense_caption, and distribution_scenarios.
Keep dense_caption factual and specific enough to drive video prompts.
Apply the fashion-vs-jewelry guardrail when embroidery, beads, metallic thread, or gemstone-like reflections are product craft rather than jewelry.
Preserve user-provided commercial inputs over inferred values.
Keep person_policy explicit, especially for fashion products and avoid_face requests.
Do not turn avoid_face into a ban on human body display when the product needs wearing, carrying, or on-foot proof.
Use templates as creative references, not as a runtime model.
If no exact sub-category template exists, use the closest category template and state the mismatch in the report.
Generate several genuinely different creative routes instead of superficial prompt variants.
Each route must show how the product appears in the first 3 seconds.
For fashion, include worn/carry/on-foot proof, silhouette or full-outline proof, and an actual occasion.
Score the nine existing dimensions as integers from 0 to 100.
Compute overall with the repository weights, not as a free-form subjective score.
Use reject/revise/shortlist/render exactly as defined in the schema.
Prefer eligible_for_render candidates before merely high-overall candidates.
Mark low feasibility, weak product clarity, and reject recommendations as render-ineligible.
Use this stage when visual risk is high or when the user asks to see still-frame probes.
Generated keyframes are evidence for review, not replacements for the original product images.
If generated previews drift from product facts, revise or reject the candidate before video generation.
Recommend exactly one candidate only when it is worth spending a video-render credit.
If no candidate clears feasibility and product-fidelity gates, set should_render=false.
Keep expected failure modes and first-render fixes concrete enough to control retry cost.
Write the markdown spec only from accepted product facts and the selected creative route.
Make the spec renderer-agnostic: it should be usable by Seedance today and by another video adapter later.
Do not include hidden reasoning; include operational checks and retry guidance.

boundary: Codex owns creative direction, fidelity constraints, scoring, and render decision.
The video adapter only executes the accepted spec and returns render outputs or failure telemetry.
Retry decisions come back through render_decision rather than being improvised inside a renderer.
